nodes.notes: Runs before the KPI refresh so the day's rates are in place when KPIs rebuild.

nodes.name: Manual Run
nodes.notes: On-demand run for backfills, demos and CLI execution. Same path as the schedule.

nodes.name: Open FX Sync Run

parameters.query:
-- Open the run ledger entry before calling anything external.
--
-- ingestion_runs is shared by every scheduled pipeline; `source` says which.
-- A crash after this point leaves a visible 'running' row rather than silence.
--
-- Window: the span of order dates that still lack a rate, widened backwards by
-- 7 days. The widening matters - if the earliest
-- unconverted order falls on a Saturday, the rate that applies to it was
-- published on the Friday, which is outside the order-date span.
WITH pending AS (
    SELECT min(order_date) AS from_date,
           max(order_date) AS to_date
    FROM salesops.fact_orders
    WHERE exchange_rate_to_usd IS NULL
      AND currency <> 'USD'
)
INSERT INTO salesops.ingestion_runs
    (batch_id, source, window_from, window_to, status, n8n_execution_id)
SELECT
    gen_random_uuid(),
    'frankfurter',
    COALESCE(
        (SELECT from_date FROM pending) - INTERVAL '7 days',
        CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 days'
    )::date,
    COALESCE((SELECT to_date FROM pending), CURRENT_DATE),
    'running',
    $1
RETURNING
    batch_id::text    AS batch_id,
    window_from::text AS window_from,
    window_to::text   AS window_to,
    run_id;

nodes.notes: Opens ingestion_runs with source='frankfurter' and computes the date window.

nodes.name: Currencies To Sync

parameters.query:
-- One row per non-USD currency the sales data actually uses.
--
-- Derived from fact_orders rather than hardcoded, so a new billing currency
-- appearing upstream is picked up without editing this workflow.
--
-- USD is excluded deliberately: Frankfurter has no USD/USD pair, and the
-- identity rate (USD -> 1.0, source 'identity') is written by the ingestion
-- pipeline. Asking a rates provider for it would be asking for a number that
-- is definitionally 1.
SELECT DISTINCT
    f.currency,
    $2::text AS window_from,
    $3::text AS window_to,
    $1::text AS batch_id
FROM salesops.fact_orders f
WHERE f.currency <> 'USD'
ORDER BY f.currency;

nodes.notes: One row per non-USD currency in the sales data. USD is the identity rate, not fetched.

nodes.name: Fetch Rates
nodes.notes: base=<CCY>&symbols=USD gives rate_to_usd directly - no inversion arithmetic. 3 attempts, 5s apart. A failure stops the run; no rate is ever invented.

nodes.name: Store Rates

parameters.query:
-- Store exactly what Frankfurter published, and nothing else.
--
-- The response is { "rates": { "2026-05-12": {"USD": 1.1738}, ... } }. Only
-- ECB business days appear - weekends and market holidays are simply absent
-- from the payload. They are NOT filled in here. This table stays a faithful
-- record of what the provider actually published; the rule for applying a rate
-- to a non-trading day lives in the attach step, where it is visible and
-- bounded.
--
-- ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING: providers revise history, and the rate we applied is
-- the rate we keep, so a report re-run next year reproduces itself. It is also
-- what makes this whole workflow safe to run repeatedly.
WITH incoming AS (
    SELECT
        (d.key)::date                        AS rate_date,
        (d.value ->> 'USD')::numeric(18,8)   AS rate_to_usd
    FROM jsonb_each($2::jsonb) AS d
    WHERE (d.value ->> 'USD') IS NOT NULL
),
stored AS (
    INSERT INTO salesops.exchange_rates (rate_date, currency, rate_to_usd, source)
    SELECT rate_date, $1, rate_to_usd, 'frankfurter'
    FROM incoming
    WHERE rate_to_usd > 0
    ON CONFLICT (rate_date, currency) DO NOTHING
    RETURNING 1
)
SELECT
    $1                                        AS currency,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM incoming)::int      AS rates_received,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM stored)::int        AS rates_inserted;

nodes.notes: Stores only the business days Frankfurter published. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.

nodes.name: Summarise Fetch
nodes.notes: Collapses per-currency results to one item so the attach step runs once.

nodes.name: Attach FX To Orders

parameters.query:
-- Attach the applicable rate to every order still lacking one.
--
-- An exact-date match is preferred, but FX is not published at weekends or on
-- market holidays while orders keep arriving. The applicable rate for a
-- non-trading day is the last one published before it - standard practice, and
-- the reason this is a LATERAL lookup rather than an equi-join.
--
-- Without it, 26 weekend dates in the current
-- dataset could never be converted and is_complete would be false forever.
--
-- The 7-day bound is the safety valve: a two-day
-- weekend is normal, a three-week gap means the feed is broken and those orders
-- must stay visibly pending rather than silently inherit a stale rate.
--
-- Only rows with no rate are touched, so a rate already applied is never
-- rewritten. The generated USD columns recompute themselves from this update -
-- nothing here writes a money value.
WITH applicable AS (
    SELECT f.order_id, r.rate_to_usd
    FROM salesops.fact_orders f
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT x.rate_to_usd
        FROM salesops.exchange_rates x
        WHERE x.currency   = f.currency
          AND x.rate_date <= f.order_date
          AND x.rate_date >= f.order_date - INTERVAL '7 days'
        ORDER BY x.rate_date DESC
        LIMIT 1
    ) AS r
    WHERE f.exchange_rate_to_usd IS NULL
),
applied AS (
    UPDATE salesops.fact_orders f
    SET exchange_rate_to_usd = a.rate_to_usd
    FROM applicable a
    WHERE f.order_id = a.order_id
    RETURNING 1
)
SELECT count(*)::int AS orders_attached FROM applied;

nodes.notes: Carry-forward lookup: last rate published on or before the order date, within 7 days. Only fills rows that have none.

nodes.name: Finalize FX Sync Run

parameters.query:
-- Close the run.
--
-- 'partial' means "completed, but the result is not fully trustworthy": here,
-- the provider returned nothing while orders were still waiting for a rate.
-- Orders left pending for a legitimate reason (no rate published that far back)
-- are reported through orders_still_pending rather than failing the run - the
-- KPI layer's fx_completeness_pct is where coverage is judged.
UPDATE salesops.ingestion_runs r
SET finished_at       = now(),
    records_received  = $2::int,
    records_accepted  = $3::int,
    records_rejected  = 0,
    records_duplicate = $2::int - $3::int,
    status = CASE
        WHEN $2::int = 0
         AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM salesops.fact_orders
                     WHERE exchange_rate_to_usd IS NULL AND currency <> 'USD')
        THEN 'partial'
        ELSE 'success'
    END
WHERE r.batch_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING
    run_id,
    batch_id::text    AS batch_id,
    window_from::text AS window_from,
    window_to::text   AS window_to,
    status,
    records_received  AS rates_received,
    records_accepted  AS rates_inserted,
    records_duplicate AS rates_already_present,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.fact_orders
      WHERE exchange_rate_to_usd IS NULL)::int AS orders_still_pending,
    round(extract(epoch FROM (finished_at - started_at))::numeric, 2) AS duration_seconds;

nodes.notes: Closes the run and reports how many orders remain unconverted.
